content: The data extraction process was conducted by one reviewer and subsequently verified by a second reviewer. Due to the variability in the interventions included in the enhanced care packages across the studies, the data were not pooled for analysis. Two reviewers independently screened 843 abstracts for eligibility, and 65 full-text articles were reviewed. One study was identified through conference abstracts, and the full-text article was obtained directly from the authors prior to publication. The PRISMA flow diagram illustrates the study selection process for inclusion in the systematic review. The abstracts from the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections were available only for the years 2014–2016. After removing duplicates, 843 records were screened, and 778 were excluded. Two records were included, and additional records were identified through other sources, such as the International AIDS Society Conference abstracts and the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections abstracts. A total of 65 full-text records were assessed for eligibility, but 63 were excluded due to reasons such as single intervention studies or non-randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Two RCTs were included in the review. Both trials excluded patients who had previously received antiretroviral therapy (ART). In the REMSTART trial, patients were selected from ambulatory care settings, while the REALITY study included hospitalized patients. The characteristics of the included studies are detailed below. Study 1: REMSTART Trial (Mfinanga et al., 2015) This open-label RCT was conducted in Tanzania and Zambia. Adult patients aged 18 years and older with advanced HIV disease (CD4 < 200 cells/mm³) were randomized to receive either an enhanced package of interventions or standard care. Intervention Group: Patients underwent serum cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) testing using a novel serum antigen assay. If the test was positive, they were offered a lumbar puncture to screen for cryptococcal meningitis. Those diagnosed with cryptococcal meningitis were treated with amphotericin B for 14 days, followed by oral fluconazole for at least 8 weeks. Patients who tested CrAg-positive but had a negative lumbar puncture or refused the procedure were treated with oral fluconazole for 10 weeks (800 mg/day for 2 weeks, followed by 400 mg/day for 8 weeks). Additionally, participants were screened for pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) using sputum GeneXpert MTB/RIF, regardless of symptoms, and all received ART initiated within 14 days. Weekly visits by lay workers were conducted during the first 4 weeks of ART to provide adherence support. In Tanzania, re-screening for TB occurred 6–8 weeks after ART initiation. Control Group: Patients received standard care, including ART initiated within 14 days and screening for pulmonary TB using sputum GeneXpert MTB/RIF. ART initiation was delayed in those testing positive for CrAg or TB, following national guidelines. Outcomes measured included all-cause mortality at 12 months, hospitalizations, ART adherence, and healthcare costs. Study 2: REALITY Trial (Hakim et al., 2017) This open-label factorial RCT was conducted in Malawi, Uganda, Zimbabwe, and Kenya. Outcomes were compared in children aged ≥5 years and adults with CD4 cell counts <100 cells/mm³ who were randomized to either standard care or an enhanced prophylaxis package. Intervention Group: Participants received ART and a fixed-dose combination (FDC) tablet containing co-trimoxazole (800/160 mg), isoniazid (300 mg), and pyridoxine (25 mg) once daily for 12 weeks. The enhanced prophylaxis package included fluconazole (100 mg/day for 12 weeks), azithromycin (500 mg/day for 5 days), and a single dose of albendazole (400 mg). After 12 weeks, fluconazole was discontinued, and patients either continued the FDC or switched to co-trimoxazole alone, depending on national guidelines. All patients underwent symptomatic screening for active TB at enrollment using a symptom checklist, sputum examination, and chest X-ray if indicated. Control Group: Participants received ART and co-trimoxazole (800/160 mg) for 12 weeks. After 12 weeks, they either continued co-trimoxazole or switched to the FDC, depending on national guidelines. In Malawi, where isoniazid was not recommended, co-trimoxazole alone was continued. Symptomatic screening for active TB was conducted at enrollment. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality at 48 weeks, new hospitalizations, new TB infections, new cryptococcal meningitis cases, new severe bacterial infections, serious adverse events, ART adherence, and CD4 cell gain. Outcomes related to new infections and serious adverse events were assessed by an independent endpoint review committee. Analysis and Risk of Bias Due to the heterogeneity of the interventions in the enhanced care packages, data extraction and analysis were conducted separately for the two studies. The overall risk of bias was rated as low for both studies. Evidence Summaries Mortality: Both trials reported all-cause mortality, with high certainty of evidence. Hospitalizations: Both studies reported hospitalization rates, with high certainty of evidence. Incident Morbidity: The REALITY trial reported the number of new serious infections in both groups, assessed by a blinded endpoint review committee. The certainty of evidence was high. Serious Adverse Events: The REALITY trial assessed severe adverse events, with high certainty of evidence. ART Adherence: Both studies reported ART adherence, which was self-reported by participants. CD4 Cell Gain: CD4 cell gain was reported in the REALITY trial, with high certainty of evidence. The findings from these studies provide robust evidence on the effectiveness of enhanced care packages in reducing mortality and improving outcomes in patients with advanced HIV disease.
